title: Swiggy and Zomato Veterans Launch AI Career Platform Profound
excerpt: Former product and technology leaders from India's top consumer tech firms raise $1.5 million to build an AI-native platform that gives every professional their own autonomous digital representative.
body:
• Former Swiggy and Zomato executives Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar have launched Profound, an AI-native career platform that assigns every professional a personal AI Rep
  • The startup raised a $1.5 million seed round backed by Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety, Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur, Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital
  • Profound uses voice AI to build deep professional profiles that go beyond static resumes, enabling intelligence-driven matching between talent and opportunities
  • The platform aims to onboard one million professionals globally within its first year

Two veterans of India’s consumer technology sector have launched Profound, an AI-first career platform that replaces the static resume with a dynamic, always-on digital representative for every working professional.

Anuj Rathi, who previously led product at Swiggy and held senior roles at Flipkart and Cleartrip, co-founded the company with Prashant Parashar, a former technology leader at Zomato, Ola and Walmart Labs. The pair spent several months in stealth mode before opening early access to their first cohort of users.

How the AI Rep Works

At its core, Profound gives each professional an AI Rep — an autonomous digital agent that starts with a 30-minute voice conversation. Unlike a LinkedIn profile or traditional resume built around job titles and skill tags, the AI Rep develops a continuously evolving understanding of a person’s experience, working style, judgment and professional ambitions.

The agent then works in the background, identifying relevant opportunities, surfacing useful connections and facilitating introductions that could lead to career moves, collaborations or mentorship.

“Just as actors have agents and athletes have managers, Profound gives each professional their own AI Rep. It learns your work and your judgment and keeps you ready for the next move.”

— Anuj Rathi, Co-Founder and CEO, Profound

Backing From India’s Tech Elite

The $1.5 million seed round drew an unusually strong roster of operator-investors. Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety and co-founder Nandan Reddy both participated, as did Pankaj Chaddah, formerly of Zomato, Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur, WhatsApp global head Kunal Shah and OfBusiness co-founder Bhuvan Gupta. Institutional capital came from Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital, two of India’s most active early-stage funds.

Rahul Chowdhri of Stellaris said the investment addresses a fundamental gap in how professional talent is discovered. “Resumes and LinkedIn profiles capture titles, not judgment,” he said. “Profound uses a voice-first, AI-native approach to build an always-on AI Rep that represents professionals with far greater depth.”

Reimagining Professional Discovery

The platform applies the same approach to hiring. Founders and hiring managers create AI Reps for open roles through natural conversations, capturing details that rarely fit into a conventional job description — working environment, team dynamics, expectations and the kind of person likely to succeed. Profound’s matching engine then uses context from both sides to make more meaningful introductions between professionals and organisations.

Pranav Pai, managing partner at 3one4 Capital, framed the problem bluntly: “The biggest constraint in hiring today is not the supply of talent but the ability to verify fit.”

A Diaspora Opportunity

For Indian professionals working globally, the platform could prove especially valuable. Cross-border career moves often founder on the gap between how candidates present themselves and what hiring managers actually need to know — cultural adaptability, domain judgment, communication style. An AI-driven system that captures these nuances through conversation rather than keywords could help bridge that divide.

What’s Next

Profound’s longer-term vision is to create an ecosystem where AI Reps interact with one another on behalf of people, roles and companies. The platform is currently in early access, with a broader beta planned later this year and a target of one million professionals globally within the next 12 months. The founding team plans to use the seed capital to strengthen engineering, product and AI capabilities.

The launch arrives at a time when India’s startup ecosystem is seeing a wave of AI-native companies founded by operators with deep platform experience. Whether Profound can convert a compelling demo into a durable professional network remains the critical test.
